items.doc: David N. Baker SI-NEA oral history (2)
items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was playing with Willis Kirk, I was playing with Chuck [Carter].

ctx.x: . . . is really quite a challenging thing physically.

It’s a challenging thing on every level. But it was a time that so much was going on in Indianapolis at the time, even though I was a beginning cellist, everybody – Elvin [Jones] was coming out there, hanging out, during the summer, playing. Chuck Carter was there. Kiger was there. Willis Kirk, the drummer the other night, was there. David Lahm had moved to Indianapolis. Paul Plummer and all the guys that had been a part of the different versions of the George Russell group were there. And so all of those cats…

[laughter] I apologized later, because it was – it was like running the gauntlet. We laugh about it now. That was just before I had quit playing the trombone, when I was still there. We’re back to switching to cello. The reason why I brought it up is because then Wes and these guys took me under [their] wing. I remember Wes telling me, when he heard me practicing – now we’ve got to back up. This same time, but it’s back just before I switched to cello, Ted Dunbar moved to town. Ted Dunbar is a wonderful guitarist…
